text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected - primary-east1 GPU pool saturated, autoscaler failing to provision capacity. Queue depth rising >1200, 5xx spike across gen endpoints. Paging SREs now.

Alyssa: seeing 504s in prod for customer-facing gen routes, latency/timeouts climbing. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'quota exceeded' on instance create.

Mike: confirmed. Cloud quota error: "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: gpu quota: 0 available in project". Looks like we hit account-level GPU quota in east1.

Priya: spike started ~2865432000, coincident with a marketing campaign. Autoscale attempted 4x scale but creations failed. Queue backlog now >1k, throttles kicking in.

Jae: Cross-region spillover should have routed to secondary-eu, is that not happening? Router shows spillover enabled but many requests stayed pinned to primary.

Alyssa: router logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:15:23Z] route decision: primary-east1 (capacity: 0) -> spillover candidate: secondary-eu (healthy)
[2026-03-15T14:15:24Z] fallback attempt -> variant-mismatch -> reject
```
Variant mismatch: primary was serving fp16-quant, secondary has int8-quant only for that model version. Router rejects due to strict variant policy.

Mike: so two problems: 1) cloud GPU quota exhausted in east1, 2) routing rejects spillover because of variant compatibility guardrail.

ops-lead: immediate mitigation steps?

Priya: propose short-term: relax variant matching for fallback (allow compatible quantized variant), enable forced spillover to secondary-eu, and spin up reserved capacity in a nearby region if quota request can't be granted quickly.

Alyssa: agree, but relaxing variant has risk of slight inference quality change. Need CS tick for impacted customers.

cs-rep: already pulling impacted customer list — roughly 12 active customers at high TPS, 3 enterprise with SLAs. We'll notify them about degraded latency and planned temporary routing.

Jae: I'll flip the router policy flag now: 
```
# temporary allow-compatible-variant
redwood-router set-policy --name fallback_variant_strictness --value permissive --expires-in 2h
```
Doing it in 60s.

deploy-bot: deploy job started: router-config-change/permit-compat-2865432200.

Alyssa: monitoring... seeing ~30% traffic now successfully failover to secondary-eu. 5xxs dropping. Queue depth in primary still high but stabilized.

Mike: manual quota request to cloud submitted (tickets/GA-7891). ETA unknown. Meanwhile requesting reserved nodes in east1 via procurement (short term allocation) + spinning up fallback pool in west1.

Priya: while we open reserve, we should also enable prefix/KV cache hits to reduce token generation load for repeat prompts. Can we toggle caching policy quickly?

Jae: toggled: 
```
redwood-config set caching.prefix_kv.enabled true
```
Expect ~15% token reduction for high-reuse prompts.

Alyssa: reminder: alerting thresholds were too low for queue length escalation; create follow-up ticket to tune alerts.

ops-lead: handoff: Priya taking lead for mitigations from here. Alyssa, can you collect timeline + commands executed for postmortem?

Alyssa: will compile timeline. Key commands/changes: router policy flip, caching toggle, reserved pool request, forced spillover.

cs-rep: sent initial customer comms to the 3 enterprise contacts: short note + ETA placeholder. No escalations yet.

Mike: monitoring CPU/GPU metrics — secondary-eu utilization climbed to 70% after spillover, latency increased ~120ms but success rate stable.

Priya: manual scaleup in west1 started as extra buffer. Also doing Canary routing to ensure model variant mapping is functionally acceptable. Running a small eval suite on sampled requests.

Alyssa: running eval results: quality delta negligible for top-k deterministic paths. Passing for immediate fallback.

Jae: router change will be reverted when capacity normalized. Set auto-revert timer for 2h.

oncall-bot: acknowledgement recorded, incident severity set to Sev2, paging continues until quota or reserved pool provisioned.

ops-lead: next steps: 1) Procure/reserve east1 capacity and raise quota escalation; 2) Postmortem: variant-policy and alert tuning; 3) Follow-up runbook to support forced spillover scenarios; 4) Customer RCA and SLA credits if needed.

Priya: handing off monitoring to Mike for the night. I'll sync with procurement and CS in morning.

Mike: noted, will watch queue and 5xxs. If queue >1500 re-escalate to exec oncall.

Alyssa: thanks all. Logging this thread into incidents tracker. Postmortem owner: Alyssa.

cs-rep: will update customers with a post-incident note once we have final root cause.

deploy-bot: router-config-change/permit-compat-2865432200 completed at 2865432255.

oncall-bot: incident status update: mitigated (traffic successfully routed to secondary-eu, queue stable). Staying in monitoring phase.

Jae: setting follow-up ticket: INT-4578 (tune fallback variant policy + alert thresholds).

Alyssa: thanks team. Closing active paging.
